cards.explanation: The answer is the Cushite woman he married. The text says Miriam and Aaron criticized Moses “…because of the Cushite woman he had married, for he had taken a Cushite wife.” That's the reason the passage gives, so I'll leave it right there. Two siblings, one complaint, and the LORD heard it (Numbers 12:2). That's a lot of weight for one complaint to carry.

The answer is that He speaks through them too. Miriam and Aaron ask, “Does the LORD speak only through Moses?” and then, “Does He not also speak through us?” They're pointing at themselves, friends. That's the whole point of the questions, and the LORD hears every word.
The answer is False. After Miriam and Aaron ask their questions, the text says, “And the LORD heard this.” That's the moment everything turns, bakers. Their conversation was not private after all.

The answer is the Tent of Meeting. The LORD says to Moses, Aaron and Miriam, “You three, come out to the Tent of Meeting.” The text says He spoke suddenly. I think I'd have dropped my whole tray of cookies.

The answer is Aaron and Miriam. The LORD came down in a pillar of cloud, stood at the entrance to the Tent, and summoned Aaron and Miriam. The two who did the talking are the two who get called forward. Moses isn't in that pair.

The answer is True, friends. The LORD says, “But this is not so with My servant Moses; he is faithful in all My house.” He calls Moses His servant and says it right in front of Aaron and Miriam. That's a strong thing to hear the LORD say about you.

The answer is clearly. The LORD says, “I speak with him face to face, clearly and not in riddles…” That's how plainly He speaks with Moses, bakers. With me, a recipe that says 'bake until done' is about as clear as a riddle.

The answer is True, friends. The text says, “So the anger of the LORD burned against them, and He departed.” That means Miriam and Aaron. This is a heavy moment, and the text doesn't soften it. After the question He asked, the anger is what comes next.

The answer is Moses, friends. Aaron turns, sees Miriam, and says to Moses, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.” He's speaking to the very one he and Miriam spoke against. That's a humbling moment.

The answer is that Aaron asks Moses not to hold their sin against them. Aaron says, “My lord, please do not hold against us this sin we have so foolishly committed.” He says 'us,' not just 'her,' bakers. He calls it a sin and a foolish one, and I think that's a hard thing to say out loud.

The answer is that Moses cries out to God to heal her. Moses cried out to the LORD, “O God, please heal her!” The one Miriam and Aaron criticized is the one who pleads for Miriam, friends. I think that says a lot about Moses, and the text has just called him “…a very humble man…” (Numbers 12:3).

The answer is seven days. The LORD says, “Let her be confined outside the camp for seven days…” The text gives it as a set number, bakers. I can't even keep a batch in the oven for a set number without checking it six times.
The answer is True, bakers. After the seven days outside the camp, the LORD says, “after that she may be brought back in.” The seven days come with an ending. That's good news.
The answer is stay put. The text says, “…the people did not move on until she was brought in again.” The whole camp waits for Miriam, friends. They stay where they are until she's back.
